_comment: WHICH EVM INSTANCE THIS PROJECT PUBLISHES, CHOSEN ON MEASURED ENDPOINT CAPABILITY,
AND THE TWO BLOCKERS THAT STOP IT SHORT OF A TRACE.
Chain-Support-Matrix.md §4 charters five EVM instances for public beta — eth, sep,
arb1, oeth and base — and says nothing about which to build first. This reading is
the answer, taken from the endpoints rather than from the ordering of that table.
-- WHY THE CAPABILITY THAT DECIDED IT IS NOT THE ONE A READER EXPECTS -------------
The obvious discriminator is `debug_traceTransaction{prestateTracer}`, and it is the
wrong one, because it is not what the recorder this project builds against asks for.
`codetracer-evm-recorder`'s `src/replay.rs` pins a `foundry-fork-db` fork at the
target block's PARENT, replays every preceding transaction in the block with a no-op
inspector, and only then replays the target with the tracing inspector. It asks a
node for account and storage reads at a past block and for nothing else — no tracer
of any kind. So the capability that decides the instance is a full ARCHIVE, and the
member of it that separates the candidates is `eth_getProof`, which `base` refuses at
depth while answering every flat state read.
That is also why the strategy token below is `replay-preceding` and not
`prestate-trace`. §1.4's `replay-preceding` row reads `Execute the block from its
parent state, in order` and requires `archive`; that is `replay.rs` sentence for
sentence. Declaring `prestate-trace` would name a tracer the producer never calls.
-- THE THREE REFUSAL CLASSES ARE KEPT APART, AND A FOURTH HAD TO BE ADDED ---------
`pruned` — present but not retained. The fourth is a TRANSPORT failure (HTTP 5xx, a
TLS timeout, a WAF block) and it is not a refusal at all: it is the run not being
answered. `endpoints[].notMeasured` is where an endpoint whose control does not
discriminate goes, rather than into any of the three.
Every endpoint below was asked `thisMethodDoesNotExist` in the same session as its
other probes, so a blind proxy cannot be read as an answer. ONE endpoint failed that
control and is reported NOT MEASURED rather than as a negative.
-- AND HTTP 400 IS NOT THE SIGNAL ON THE WINNING ENDPOINT -------------------------
`eth.drpc.org` returns HTTP **400** with a well-formed JSON-RPC error body for every
refusal, including `-32601`. A prober that classified on the HTTP code would read
every one of its refusals as a transport failure and every one of its distinctions as
lost. Read the body.
measuredBy: curl 8.x and python3 urllib over plain HTTP from the workstation; no chain CLI and no key

prestateStrategyBasis: DERIVED FROM THE RECORDER'S CODE, not chosen from §1.4's preference order.
transactions.iter().enumerate()` committing every transaction below the target's
index, then switches inspectors for the target. Its cost is O(block) per block, which
is §1.4's own cost column for this row.
THE PRESTATE-CLASS CONSEQUENCE, STATED RATHER THAN LEFT TO FALL OUT. The ledger that
groups chains by prestate class carries the `evm` row as `undetermined`, and an
`undetermined` row joins no class at all. Declaring `replay-preceding` puts the EVM
family in a class whose other reachable member is Flow — §1.4 calls
`replay-preceding` "the universal fallback for account-model chains" and both chains
have a reachable archive. Declaring `prestate-trace` instead would have paired it with
Starknet or PolkaVM. The pair is the decision; this is the half of it this reading
why: It is the only endpoint probed that serves the COMPLETE read-set `replay-preceding`
needs — balance, nonce, code, storage, PROOF and call, at depth — and it serves it to
genesis. `base` answers five of the six and refuses the sixth; `publicnode` refuses
all six as policy; Sepolia has no free archive at all on either endpoint that answered.
And `eth` is §4's own Reference chain, so the instance measurement and the charter
agree. That is a coincidence worth stating as one: the choice was made on the
`eth_getProof` column, and it would have selected `eth` over `base` even if §4 had

rejected.why: NO FREE ARCHIVE, measured on both endpoints that answered its control. `publicnode` returns `-32603 state at block #3502093 is pruned` for balance, nonce, code and storage alike, and `-32602 distance to target block exceeds maximum proof window` for `eth_getProof`; `1rpc.io/sepolia` answers balance and code at that depth and refuses nonce as pruned and proof as beyond the window. A chain whose prestate is not served cannot be replayed from its parent state, whatever its transaction count.

Free archive for every FLAT state read at block 33,554,432 — balance, nonce, code, storage and `eth_call` all answered — and `eth_getProof` refused with `-32603 no state found for block number 33554432`. The refusal is specific to the proof path while the flat reads answer, which is a real and narrow endpoint property rather than a blanket absence, and it is enough: `foundry-fork-db` is the component that would meet it.

MEASURABLY THE CHEAPEST SUBJECT AND THE WRONG SEMANTICS. 2-9 transactions per block against Ethereum's 249-359 — an order of magnitude less replay work per block, which matters because the site's curated ingest needs a whole block traced (see `blockers.B3`). But the recorder replays with mainnet revm (`ctx.build_mainnet_with_inspector`), and Arbitrum Nitro has its own gas model, an ArbOS system transaction at index 0 and L1 data fees that mainnet revm does not model. Publishing its rows as T2 real-VM traces would be a fidelity claim nothing measured. Recorded here because the cost argument is genuine and someone will re-derive it.
30-52 transactions per block, between Arbitrum and Ethereum, and the same semantic objection as arb1: an OP deposit transaction at index 0 and an L1 fee term mainnet revm does not carry.

NOT A CHARTERED INSTANCE. It answers archive reads at 0x1000000 and its control is clean, and it cannot serve as a SECOND, independent EVM subject — it is the same chain family and therefore the same prestate-class ledger row as `eth`. Probed to keep the row honest, not as a candidate.

twoSidedControl: AGREEMENT ACROSS METHODS AND DISAGREEMENT ACROSS DEPTH, because either alone is
satisfiable by a constant. At six depths — 1,000,000 / 4,370,000 / 12,965,000 /
equal `eth_getBalance` and `eth_getTransactionCount` at the same block, 6 of 6; and
the six balances are 6 DISTINCT values and the six nonces 6 distinct values
(90 / 654 / 715 / 885 / 1553 / 5956). A blind or cached answer satisfies the first
The proof's own node count rising 4 -> 5 -> 8 -> 9 with the age of the trie is a
third, unasked-for corroboration: the depth of the account trie at each block is not
a quantity a constant response carries.

what: `eth_getStorageAt` at depth returns HTTP 403 for User-Agent `Python-urllib/3.11` and
HTTP 200 for an ABSENT User-Agent, for `reqwest/0.12` and for `curl/8.5.0` — while
`eth_chainId` returns 200 for `Python-urllib/3.11` in the same session. So the gate is
joint on method and agent, and the sequence 60/60 403, then 60/60 200, then 60/60 403
rules out a rate limit or a transient.
WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: a prober using a default-UA HTTP client
reads this as `the archive is policy-refused`, which is the same sentence `publicnode`
returns for a genuinely different reason. It cost this session one wrong reading. The
recorder is unaffected — alloy sends reqwest's UA, measured 200 — and so is a Node
producer, measured 200 on node 22.23.2 `fetch` with and without an explicit UA.

that refuses a nonexistent method and a real one identically cannot distinguish

evidence that the method is absent OR that it is gated.

B1.verdict: TERMINAL for a traced row, and it is in a third repository
B1.subject: codetracer-evm-recorder
measured: THE BINARY HAS ONE SUBCOMMAND AND IT IS NOT REPLAY. `codetracer-evm-recorder --help`
lists `record` and `help`; `replay --help` answers `error: unrecognized subcommand
'replay'`. `src/main.rs`'s `enum Commands` has exactly one variant, `Record(RecordArgs)`,
and `RecordArgs` takes a `.sol` path, `--out-dir`, `--function`, `--from` and `--value` —
no transaction hash, no RPC URL, no address. The README documents
`codetracer-evm-recorder replay <tx-hash> --out-dir <dir>`.
AND IT IS NOT A MISSING SUBCOMMAND, WHICH IS THE READING TO AVOID. `src/replay.rs`'s
`replay_transaction` returns `inspector::ExecutionData`; `recorder.rs`'s two writing
entry points are `record_from_structlog` and `record_from_structlog_multi_contract`,
which take STRUCTLOGS. Nothing converts one to the other. Swept over the whole crate:
the only mention of `replay` outside `src/replay.rs` itself is `pub mod replay;` in
`src/lib.rs`. So `ExecutionData` reaches no container writer, and the gap is a join
rather than a route.
ACROSS EVERY PUBLISHED BRANCH, NOT JUST THE TIP. `git show <branch>:src/main.rs | grep
Replay` over all 13 `refs/remotes/origin/*`: zero hits. And the 10 commits that landed
on `origin/dev` during the build touch `.github/workflows/*`, `flake.nix`, `repro.lock`
and `repro.nim` and NO `.rs` file, so the build at 64cb02f is the current tip for this
purpose.
POSITIVE CONTROL, so the absence is not read off a broken build: the same binary
records `examples/ERC20.sol` — solc 0.8.33, anvil 1.5.1-dev from its own devShell,
878 struct log entries fetched, a 143,360-byte `ERC20.ct` written, rc 0. The recorder
works. What it has no route to is a transaction it did not itself create.
B1.remedy: Join `ExecutionData` to a container writer and give it a subcommand. It is work in `codetracer-evm-recorder`, and that repository's own roadmap owns it.
B1.notOurBranch: This reading was taken from `codetracer-evm-recorder`; nothing in it was changed.

B2.verdict: would block the structlog route even once B1's wiring existed — so the remedy chooses the revm route for a measured reason
measured: `src/trace_fetcher.rs` asks for `debug_traceTransaction` with the DEFAULT tracer: a
`GethDebugTracingOptions` carrying a populated `config` and no `tracer`. Five free
Ethereum-mainnet endpoints, each with its control in the same session:
eth.drpc.org                 POLICY   code 5 wrapping -32602, `Tracer object with 'tracer' param is required`
ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com  ABSENT   -32601
1rpc.io/eth                  POLICY   -32600 `Method debug_traceTransaction not allowed`
rpc.ankr.com/eth             NOT MEASURED — its control does not discriminate
eth.llamarpc.com             NOT MEASURED — HTTP 525, a transport failure
So zero of the three measurable endpoints serve it, in two distinct classes.
THE CONSEQUENCE IS A DESIGN INPUT AND NOT A SECOND WALL. `replay.rs`'s revm route needs
no tracer at all — only the archive reads `eth.drpc.org` serves in full, proved above.
So B1's remedy is to join `ExecutionData` to a writer, NOT to route the structlog
fetcher, and that ordering is measured rather than preferred.

B3.verdict: would block an all-untraced Ethereum snapshot from reaching the site even with a conforming tree
measured: `client/src/static_export.nim:621-623` ingests every `client/fixtures/chain/*/` with
`scope: isCurated`, and `src/blocktracer/chain/ingest.nim:1362-1380` RAISES for any row
in the published window whose outcome is neither `replayed` nor `divergent`.
`curationWindow` (`ingest.nim:407`) has two shapes and an Ethereum mainnet capture with
no recording reaches neither: with `recorded.len == 0` it looks for maximal runs of
consecutive blocks that settled NO transaction, and on Ethereum mainnet there are none,
so `runs.len == 0`, `found` stays false, and the ingest raises.
WHAT THAT MEANS FOR THE WINDOW SIZE ONCE B1 IS FIXED: the cheapest publishable subject
is ONE WHOLE BLOCK traced, not one transaction. `replay-preceding` replays indices
0..k-1 for each target k, so a block of N transactions costs ~N²/2 transaction
executions. At Ethereum's measured 249-359 that is 31,000-64,000 executions for one
block. This is the number that makes the transactionsPerBlock table above a cost rather
than a statistic, and it is why `arb1`'s 2-9 was worth recording even though its
semantics rule it out.
